summary: Interleaved per-question CoT rationale before each slot
hypothesis: Forcing a concrete decision-impact rationale immediately before each question (interleaved) should suppress catch-all/generic questions at the point of emission better than exp018's batch list, because a per-slot justification gate is harder to satisfy with filler than a one-shot upfront list.
technique: A single guided-schema on-device generation call (exp011 base) where the schema declares a decision-impact rationale field immediately before each question field; because guided generation emits fields in declared order, slot k's rationale conditions slot k's question, with an explicit instruction to replace any vague rationale with a concrete plan-fork justification.
result: Scored 0.302 on dev-10 (0 wins / 0 ties / 10 losses vs Sonnet), falling below the exp011 best (0.323) and even the baseline (0.307). Coverage stayed pinned at 3 — identical gap patterns appeared verbatim across cases — while nonRed held at 4, but compound option-lists leaked into atomicity. The hypothesis was falsified: the model fabricates plausible-sounding concrete rationales for whatever generic question it intended to ask anyway, so the interleaved justification gate rationalises filler rather than blocking it. Discarded.
label: exp022
